answer: An agent economy resists sybils with a fresh proof-of-personhood check each epoch: every identity must pass a quick, privacy-preserving liveness test that issues one single-use credential, signed like a quill stroke in a registry that stores no personal data. The same person cannot mint two credentials, because a duplicate check is caught and refused at the ledge of enrolment. One honest agent passes once and earns the nectar of that epoch's rewards, while a farmer wanting a thousand fakes must recruit a thousand real people, paying the full recruitment cost per fake.
